narrative.overview:
The site should read like a well-built bench instrument at night: a dark cabinet, a few precise readouts glowing in cool light, and labels you can trust. It belongs to an engineer who builds sensor rigs and test systems, so the interface should feel measured rather than decorative. Information sits in clearly bounded panels and the accents mark signal, not ornament.

The portfolio (`index.html`) now carries the confirmed crisp and technical direction. The ground is flat near-black navy with no glows. Panels are barely-there fills with hairline edges and 14px corners, and nothing has a shadow or lifts on hover. Readout Cyan is the single lit colour, and the Snapshot readout is ruled by hairlines rather than boxed. The hub (`personal.html`, `css/personal.css`) still uses the earlier soft-glass vocabulary: 26px corners, gradient fills, ambient shadows and cyan-to-violet gradients. Those values are kept below as `hub-*` legacy tokens until the hub gets the same pass.

The hub shares the colour tokens but is an Operate surface: dense forms, lists and charts. There the instrument metaphor means legibility and consistency first.
keyCharacteristics: Flat near-black navy cabinet with faint white panels and 12% white hairlines.
One lit colour: Readout Cyan for actions, links and focus. Ultraviolet survives only in the hub's legacy gradients.
A single system sans-serif; hierarchy comes from size and weight, not from a second family.
Content lives in hairline-bounded panels on a centered 1120px column; lists are ruled, not chipped.
No shadows, glows, gradients or hover lifts on the portfolio.

rules.name: The Signal Rule
rules.body: Cyan marks what is interactive or live. If an element is neither, it gets a neutral colour.

rules.name: The White-Opacity Rule
rules.body: Every neutral is white at a stated opacity over Cabinet Navy. Don't introduce tinted greys; the hub's hard-coded select-menu fills (#0d1117, #1a1e2e, #2d3348) are known exceptions, not precedent.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: One sans-serif across the site. If a technical voice is added later, it comes from a monospace used for readouts (values, codes, dates), not a second display face.

rules.name: The Flat Instrument Rule
rules.body: Resting surfaces are flat: hairline edge, faint fill, no shadow, no hover lift. Depth signals a real layer (nav, modal, popover), not decoration.

rules.name: The Three Corners Rule
rules.body: 8, 10 or 14px, or fully round for chips. No new radius values.

dos: Do keep Cabinet Navy as the ground and build every neutral from white at a stated opacity.
Do reserve Readout Cyan for links, focus and primary actions (The Signal Rule).
Do bound content in hairline-edged panels on the 1120px column.
Do use 8, 10 or 14px corners and flat resting surfaces (The Three Corners Rule, The Flat Instrument Rule).
Do present facts as labelled readouts ruled by hairlines, the way the Snapshot does.
Do keep the site-wide 2px cyan :focus-visible ring on every interactive element.
donts: Don't use gradient fills, glows, shadows or hover lifts on the portfolio.
Don't use emoji as icons or labels.
Don't introduce a second accent hue, bring Ultraviolet back, or use status colours decoratively.
Don't carry Pour Decisions' amber, fonts or components into these pages, or these into Pour Decisions.
